slim.summary: Two hard failures make the feature unusable as submitted: the new module imports a nonexistent `cosmos_approval` module on startup, and both `accept()` and `reject()` import an undefined `assert_pen` symbol from `cosmos_ccr`. There is also a state-machine bug where reproposing the same content-addressed SHA resets it to `PROPOSED`, defeating the intended one-decision-per-SHA behavior.

findings.message: `open_registry()` imports `ApprovalGate` from `cosmos_approval`, but that module is not present in the current tree. As written, every CLI subcommand (`propose`, `accept`, `list`) and any programmatic call through `open_registry()` will fail with `ModuleNotFoundError` before the registry can be used.

`accept()` imports `assert_pen` from `cosmos_ccr`, but `cosmos_ccr.py` does not define that symbol. The same bad import is repeated in `reject()` at line 194. Both decision paths therefore raise `ImportError` immediately, so no proposal can ever be accepted or rejected.

The fold logic reopens an already-decided proposal whenever the same SKILL.md is proposed again. Because `SKILL_PROPOSED` unconditionally overwrites `s["proposed"][sha]` back to `state="PROPOSED"`, resubmitting identical content bypasses the `ALREADY_DECIDED` guard in `_proposal()`. That lets a previously rejected SHA be reconsidered and lets an already accepted SHA be re-accepted to bump the active version without any content change.
